intro_html: Order a turkey Reuben at a deli and you get turkey, sauerkraut, Swiss, and Russian dressing on grilled rye. Order fourteen of them and you get a bill you do not want to look at. This bakes the whole sandwich into a pan instead: buttered rye cubes on the bottom, turkey and kraut and Swiss layered through, dressing whisked in. Each serving lands at 623 calories with 42 grams of protein for about $1.96.
cost_closing_html: About $1.96 a serving for a deli sandwich you would pay four times that for at the counter. Sauerkraut is one of the cheapest things in the store and it is the ingredient that makes this taste like the real thing.
shop_smart: A single loaf of rye covers this whole pan. Marked-down day-old rye is actually better here, because stale bread holds its structure under the dressing instead of turning to paste.
Canned sauerkraut costs less than the refrigerated bags and works fine once it is squeezed dry. That squeeze is not optional; wet kraut will flood the pan.
Swiss cheese is the biggest line item. Buy it by whichever pack has the lowest price per ounce and shred it yourself rather than buying slices.
Skip bottled Russian dressing. Mayonnaise, ketchup, and chopped dill pickles make the same thing from items already in your fridge.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cube the rye bread, toss it with the melted butter and the caraway seeds, and toast it on a sheet pan at 350F for 10 minutes until the edges dry out.
Drain the sauerkraut and squeeze it dry in a clean towel. Wring it hard, then wring it again, because kraut holds more liquid than it looks like it does.
Whisk the mayonnaise with the Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, chopped dill pickles, salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Spread half the toasted rye cubes across a greased 9x13 pan, then layer on the sliced turkey breast, the squeezed sauerkraut, and half the shredded Swiss.
Spoon the dressing evenly over the layers, then top with the remaining rye cubes and press the whole thing down firmly so it compacts.
Cover with foil and bake at 350F for 30 minutes, then uncover, add the rest of the Swiss, and bake 15 minutes more until browned and bubbling.
Rest 15 minutes before portioning so the layers hold together on the spatula.
portion_html: Weigh the pan, subtract the empty pan weight, and divide by 14. Cut squares to that number and lift them flat so the rye layers stay stacked. Each serving comes to 623 calories and 42 grams of protein.
upsell_html: A deli Reuben for about $1.96 a serving, and this is one of many. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons, calculators, and tools, for $1 a month.

head.description: Turkey Reuben casserole meal prep: rye bread, turkey, sauerkraut, and Swiss baked with a homemade Russian dressing. 623 calories, 42g protein, about $1.96 a serving.
head.keywords: turkey reuben casserole, reuben bake, sauerkraut casserole, deli sandwich casserole, high protein meal prep, budget dinner
steps: Toss cubed rye with melted butter and caraway seeds and toast at 350F for 10 minutes.
Drain and wring the sauerkraut completely dry.
Whisk the mayonnaise with Dijon, Worcestershire, garlic powder, chopped dill pickles, salt, and pepper.
Layer half the rye, the turkey, the kraut, and half the Swiss in a greased 9x13 pan, then spoon the dressing over and top with the rest of the rye.
Bake covered at 350F for 30 minutes, uncover, add the last Swiss, bake 15 minutes more, rest 15 minutes, and portion into 14 containers.
